attributes.residual: NOT CLOSABLE THIS RUN, with the blocker now named per cluster instead of per function. Measured from the raw objects: 582/582 instructions, THIRTY-TWO differing words (not three - the --ops clusters list only the unpaired/replaced rows, and the ~29-word recolor web is invisible to that view). CLUSTER A, window [0x740,0x744): ours `lwz r0,1624(r31)` then `addi r29,r31,1388`, retail the reverse. STEP 0 PASSES - check_permutation_dependences accepts order [1,0] in its strictest form - and the swap ALONE reproduces the retail bytes for that window exactly. This cluster is rule-ready today. CLUSTER B, the form pair at +0x8b0: ours decodes ('li', 27, 0), retail decodes ('copy', 29, 30). Destinations r27 vs r29 DIFFER, so equivalent_copy_form refuses it by name as a recolor, in every proof mode including the new one; the across-calls extension does not touch this and the site remains blocked on LZ's v2 combined pass. CLUSTER C IS NOT A PERMUTATION AT ALL, and this is the finding that matters most: ours `addi r29,r4,200` at +0x8c0 followed by `li r4,0`, and STEP 0 REFUSES the swap with `breaks def-use chains: [(0, ('g', 4))]` - our addi READS r4 and the li WRITES it, so exchanging them is a genuine WAR hazard, not a schedule choice. The swap also does not reach the target: retail's word at +0x8c4 is `addi r28,r28,200`, a RECOLORED instruction, against our `addi r29,r4,200`. Cluster C is therefore a positional artifact of the surrounding register-web difference, exactly C1's refuted class. HANDOFF: camera_mode_level needs (i) LZ's v2 combined form+renaming pass for cluster B and (ii) a recolor that subsumes cluster C, after which only cluster A remains as a real permutation. Do not derive a permutation window for cluster C; it will refuse, correctly.
